🚨 U.S. ARMY PREPARES FOR FIRST MILITARY EXECUTIONS SINCE 1961

The U.S. Army has quietly laid the groundwork to resume military executions for the first time in 65 years.

An internal Army plan called “OPERATION RESOLUTE JUSTICE” directs officials to prepare for the execution of military death-row prisoners if President Trump gives final authorization.

🔹 Four prisoners currently sit on military death row.

🔹 The Army would coordinate with the Federal Bureau of Prisons to transfer condemned prisoners from Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, to the federal execution facility in Terre Haute, Indiana.

🔹 The plan requires the Army to be capable of carrying out an execution within 150 days of presidential approval.

🔹 Under the Uniform Code of Military Justice, a military death sentence cannot be carried out until the President personally approves it.

One case clearly looming over this is former Army Major Nidal Hasan, convicted and sentenced to death for the 2009 Fort Hood massacre that killed 13 people and wounded 32 others.

In September 2025, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth formally requested that President Trump sign Hasan’s death warrant, according to an article published by the Army’s own Judge Advocate General’s Corps. (lineofdeparture.army.mil)

The Army says these preparations are not themselves evidence that Trump has ordered executions, noting that execution-planning exercises have occurred periodically for roughly 20 years. As of the latest reporting, Trump has not issued the required execution order. (www-cdn.abcnews.com)

⚠️ THE HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE

The U.S. military has executed no one since 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was hanged at Fort Leavenworth.

Now, 65 years later, the infrastructure and procedures are being put into position again under an operation literally named:

OPERATION RESOLUTE JUSTICE.
